evidence: html_website/main.py: generate_module_website() is a 400-line function that simultaneously parses curriculum elements, builds sidebar HTML, embeds ~200 lines of inline JavaScript, constructs question interaction logic per-type, and writes the output file — five to six distinct responsibilities in a single body

publish/utils.py: file mixes flattening logic (flatten_module, flatten_published), cleaning logic (clean_published), four copy functions (copy_labs_and_dashboards, copy_slides, copy_slides_to_modules, copy_practice_tests), and a full category-reorganization algorithm (reorganize_to_categories) in one file, covering the entire pipeline post-generation

batch_processing/main.py (per persisted output): contains process_module_to_pdf, process_module_to_txt, process_module_to_mp3, generate_all_outputs, clear_all_outputs — broad format dispatch plus orchestration in one module

legacy_import/main.py: process_slides() duplicates the entire chapter-to-module lookup + copy loop for full-slides and notes-slides sub-types; the repeated structural pattern (extract chapter, map to module, ensure_module_exists, build output filename, copy/log, handle errors) appears in nearly identical form twice within the same function body (200+ lines)

scripts/publish_all.py step 5 and step 6 share the same --skip-copy-extras gate, but step 6 has no dedicated --skip-slides guard — the pairing is implicit and likely to silently skip slides when the user only intends to skip labs

format_conversion/main.py convert_file() uses a large if/elif chain on a string key (conversion_key = f'{input_ext}->{output_format_lower}') rather than a dispatch table, making the pattern data-driven in name only

scripts/flatten_published.py, generate_all_outputs.py, generate_module_website.py, generate_syllabus_renderings.py, publish_course.py, renumber_questions.py are all CLI entry points invoked via subprocess from publish_all.py; the 'orphaned' signal is a false positive — they are shell-entry-point scripts, not library modules

html_website/main.py: create_section() is a nested helper function defined inside generate_module_website(); it is only used locally, but the nesting adds cognitive overhead without clarity benefit — a module-level private function would be cleaner

content_processing/main.py: process_questions_file() does file reading, regex-based format detection, question extraction, reformatting, and writing — five concerns in ~60 lines, though they share a single coherent pipeline
design_coherence.issues_preventing_higher_score: The top issue is generate_module_website() being a 400-line god function that inlines JavaScript, HTML construction, and question-type dispatch together. The secondary issue is publish/utils.py being a catch-all for every post-generation pipeline operation. Both are addressable by splitting responsibilities into focused modules.

strengths: The layered module architecture (layer 0-4) is well-conceived and enforced — low-level converters do not import orchestration modules
Scripts are correctly kept as thin CLI orchestrators that delegate to src.* modules
lab_manual/main.py cleanly separates parse_lab_elements, _process_lab_content, and render_lab_manual with clear single-purpose abstractions
validation/main.py decomposes into focused helpers (_validate_module_outputs, _validate_syllabus_outputs, validate_published) that each own one concern
module_organization/main.py has tight, coherent functions — every public function does exactly one thing
design_coherence.issue_character: The dominant issue is concentrated complexity: a small number of files (html_website/main.py, publish/utils.py, legacy_import/main.py) accumulate multiple unrelated responsibilities, while the majority of the codebase maintains good single-responsibility discipline.
design_coherence.score_rationale: Most modules demonstrate good design coherence — thin scripts, focused helpers, clear layer separation. However, html_website/main.py's generate_module_website() function conflates HTML construction, JavaScript embedding, per-question-type rendering, and file I/O into a single 400-line body. publish/utils.py serves as an operational grab-bag for six distinct pipeline operations. legacy_import/main.py duplicates a structural copy pattern twice in process_slides(). These represent design debt in high-traffic pipeline paths rather than domain complexity, placing the score in the low-70s range.

issues.summary: generate_module_website() is a 400-line god function mixing HTML construction, JavaScript embedding, and per-question-type dispatch
evidence: Single function handles: curriculum element processing, audio/text file lookup, sidebar HTML assembly, question parsing per type (multiple_choice, free_response, true_false, matching), progress bar HTML, ~200 lines of inline JavaScript, and file output
Nested create_section() helper defined inside the function body
issues.suggestion: Extract question rendering into a render_question(q) function, move JavaScript to an external file or config constant, extract sidebar_html construction to build_sidebar(), and move the per-type HTML generators into utils.py. The top-level function should orchestrate, not implement.

issues.summary: publish/utils.py is a pipeline catch-all mixing flattening, cleaning, four copy operations, and category reorganization
evidence: File contains: clean_directory, copy_directory_contents, flatten_module, flatten_published, clean_published, copy_labs_and_dashboards, copy_slides, copy_slides_to_modules, copy_exams, copy_practice_tests, reorganize_to_categories
Six distinct pipeline operations with no shared abstraction between them
issues.suggestion: Split into at minimum: copy_ops.py (copy_labs_and_dashboards, copy_slides*, copy_practice_tests, copy_exams), structure_ops.py (flatten_*, clean_*), and reorganize.py (reorganize_to_categories). Keep utils.py for truly shared helpers (clean_directory, copy_directory_contents).

issues.summary: legacy_import/main.py duplicates the chapter-map/copy/log pattern for full-slides and notes-slides within a single function
evidence: process_slides() contains two near-identical loops: one for slides_full_dir and one for slides_notes_dir, each ~75 lines with identical structure: extract chapter number, map to module, ensure_module_exists, build output filename, dry_run branch, copy, log, error handling
The only meaningful difference is the output_filename suffix ('slides-full' vs 'slides-notes')
issues.suggestion: Extract a _process_slide_dir(source_dir, slide_type, chapter_mapping, course_root, dry_run) helper and call it twice from process_slides().

issues.summary: publish_all.py silently skips slides when --skip-copy-extras is used, because step 6 shares step 5's gate with no independent flag
evidence: Lines 237-243: step 6 (copy slides and practice tests) is gated by `if not args.skip_copy_extras:` — the same flag as step 5 (copy labs and dashboards)
A user passing --skip-copy-extras intending to skip labs will also silently skip slides and practice tests, despite no --skip-slides flag existing
issues.suggestion: Add a dedicated --skip-slides flag (or document explicitly that --skip-copy-extras covers all three copy operations). At minimum add a comment on step 6 noting its shared gate.

issues.summary: format_conversion/main.py uses a string-keyed if/elif dispatch rather than a data-driven dispatch table
evidence: convert_file() builds conversion_key = f'{input_ext}->{output_format_lower}' then has 9 elif branches, each importing a specific converter
Adding a new format requires editing the dispatch chain, not registering in a table
issues.suggestion: Replace the if/elif chain with a dict: CONVERTERS = {'md->pdf': convert_markdown_to_pdf, ...} and do handler = CONVERTERS.get(conversion_key); if not handler: raise ValueError(...); handler(input_file, output_file).

root_causes: html_website module grew organically as a single script and was never refactored into components
publish/utils.py became a landing zone for migrated script logic without a clear ownership boundary
legacy_import code was likely written once for full-slides, then copy-pasted for notes-slides
likely_symptoms: dc-04 is a usability defect, not a design defect — could be re-scoped to interface clarity
possible_false_positives: scripts/*.py being flagged as 'orphaned' — they are intentional CLI entry points
